display.title: Elul: Pressing the Total Button on the Year
display.summary_short: Elul is when we add up the whole year's mitzvos, like pressing 'total' on a calculator, resolve to leave our aveiros behind, and 'smile back' at Hashem, Who is close like a king in the field.
display.summary_long: A teshuvah talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given in the month of Elul. Uncle Yossi explains that Elul is the climax and wind-up of the whole year. All year we have been adding mitzvos: learning Torah, davening, giving tzedakah and honoring parents. In Elul we press the 'total' button, like on a calculator, and take inventory of our thoughts, words and deeds, checking that they are truly mitzvos and not aveiros. If we listened to the yetzer hara during the year, we now resolve never to repeat it and to do more mitzvos than ever, and Hashem, in His mercy, erases the aveiros so only good deeds remain on our record before Rosh Hashanah, when we ask for a good and sweet year. Citing the Alter Rebbe's parable in Likkutei Torah of the King in the field, he calls these the days of goodwill: Hashem is right there smiling at us, so the order of the month is to smile back, greeting Him with trust and joy.
display.lesson: Use Elul to add up your year honestly, leave the aveiros behind, and greet Hashem with joy while He is so close.
